title: Backpacker twists knee in a standing fall on technical terrain

source.title: Case Study: Injured Knee in the Wind River Mountains

classification.acuity_basis: Usable knee; braced and assisted walk-out same day.

presentation.summary: Five miles into a loop, a hiker falls from standing onto his side on technical terrain and injures his right knee.

plan: improvised knee brace, walk out with assistance and shared pack weight
clean, irrigate and dress hand abrasions
teaching_points: Usability, not diagnosis: usable -> pain control and brace/tape; unusable -> immobilize and evacuate.
Check CSM before and after splinting.
RICE: ice 20-40 min every 2-4 h, compression, elevation.

outcome.summary: Turned back, reached car at dusk with assistance.

must_ask: can you put weight on it?
does the knee lock or give way?
eval.must_escalate: Immobilize and evacuate if unable to bear weight.
must_not_recommend: continuing deeper into the loop on an injured knee

lay_queries: I fell and hurt my knee and it's swelling
can I hike out on a hurt knee

title: Handhold breaks: climber swings into wall with deformed ankle, abroad

source.title: Case Study: A Climbing Fall in Greece

classification.acuity_basis: Deformed, unusable ankle; carry-out to EMS.

context.distance_to_care: 0.5 km carry + 1.2 km 4WD to parking lot EMS; EU emergency number 112

presentation.summary: A handhold breaks and a climber swings feet first into the wall, screaming in pain. Bystanders crowd in; 112 caller struggles to give the island name.

assessment: unusable left ankle injury; cannot walk
plan: call local EMS (112), meet at parking lot
padded rigid splint of foot and lower leg
teaching_points: Slow the scene down and complete a full assessment.
Include and support the patient; manage bystanders.
Splint: padded, adjustable, rigid; immobilize bones above and below the joint; check CSM.
Know the local emergency number and precise location when traveling.

must_ask: can she feel and move her toes?
is the foot warm and pink?
do you know your exact location / local emergency number?
eval.must_escalate: Call local EMS (112 in EU) and evacuate.

lay_queries: climber fell and her ankle is bent the wrong way
what's the emergency number in Greece

title: Engorged tick found on day 6 of an Appalachian Trail hike

source.title: Case Study: Embedded Tick while Backpacking

classification.acuity_basis: Engorged tick in Lyme-endemic area: clinic within 72 h for prophylaxis.

presentation.summary: During a break a hiker finds a small engorged tick embedded in his leg.
presentation.chief_complaint: there is a tick on me
exam_findings: small engorged embedded tick on leg

plan: remove with tweezers close to skin, steady pull
see clinician within 72 h for prophylaxis
teaching_points: Lyme disease is the most common US tick-borne illness.
No ointments, chemicals, or heat to remove ticks.
Watch for rash/ulcer, aches, joint pain, fever.
Engorged tick in endemic area: see a provider within 72 h for prophylaxis; anyone with rash, aches or fever should be evacuated.
Prevention: long sleeves/pants, DEET/picaridin/IR3535, permethrin on clothing, tick checks twice daily.

decision_points.question: Evacuate now?
decision_points.source_decision: No; clinic on exit next day

outcome.summary: Finished trip; clinic prescribed prophylactic antibiotic.

must_recognize: engorged tick in endemic area warrants prophylaxis consideration
must_ask: how long was it attached / is it engorged?
eval.must_escalate: See a clinician within 72 h; sooner if rash or fever.
must_not_recommend: burning, smothering, or twisting off the tick

lay_queries: found a tick stuck in my leg
how do I get a tick out
do I need antibiotics after a tick bite
